headline: 2 Bangladeshis killed in Houthi missile attack at Riyadh airport, 4 in ICU

members.title: 2 Bangladeshis killed in Houthi missile attack at Riyadh airport, 4 in ICU
members.lead: Two Bangladeshis were killed in an attack by Houthi rebels at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Four other Bangladeshis injured in the attack are receiving treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of King Khalid Hospital in Riyadh. Foreign Affairs State Minister Shama Obaed Islam shared the information while responding to questions from journalists at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Sunday afternoon. Earlier, when the Houthis launched an attack, a Bangladeshi was killed. Now, two more have been killed, the state minister said. Referring to the 14 Bangladeshis who have already died in the Middle East conflict, Shama Obaed said, “We hope this disaster will end and these attacks will stop. It is extremely painful to accept such deaths.” . In a statement on Saturday’s attack in Riyadh, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said a missile struck Terminal-3 of King Khalid International Airport at around 3:20pm on Saturday. Passengers from Bangladesh and several other countries were waiting at the terminal at the time. Two Bangladeshi nationals were killed in the incident. They were Md Shahed Ahmed of Madla village in Shahjahanpur upazila of Bogura and Md Nasrullah Badarpuri of Badarpur village in Nangalkot upazila of Cumilla. Diplomatic sources in Riyadh said Bangladeshi passengers travelling with US-Bangla Airlines, Saudia and Riyadh Air were at the airport during the attack. Among the passengers who were not injured, 17 are staying at the Marriott Hotel, 25 at the Radisson Hotel and 40 at the residential hall of Princess Nourah University. . Four injured Bangladeshis are currently receiving treatment in the ICU of King Khalid Hospital. Two other passengers who were not injured are also staying there with them. Shama Obaed said, “We are deeply saddened by this incident. members.title: 8 flights from Dhaka cancelled; Biman to update on 2 on Monday
members.lead: Eight flights from Dhaka to Riyadh have so far been cancelled following an attack on King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital. Apart from the cancellations, Biman Bangladesh Airlines will provide details about two of its flights at noon on Monday. Biman Bangladesh Airlines announced the information in separate press releases issued on Sunday. . On Saturday night, Bangladesh time, the Iran-backed Houthi armed group in Yemen attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia. It was the third attack on the airport this week. Following the incident, airport operations were suspended and all flights were diverted. Shortly after the incident, Biman Bangladesh Airlines announced the suspension of flights BG339 and BG340. In a statement issued on Sunday, the national flag carrier said the airport authorities had extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport until 9:00 pm UTC on 11 October. In Bangladesh time, the suspension will remain in effect until 3:00 am on Monday. . As of Sunday afternoon, the eight cancelled flights included two operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, one by US-Bangla Airlines, three by Saudia and two by Riyadh Air. According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), a total of 2,951 passengers were booked on these flights. Reporting the suspension of flights at Riyadh’s international airport, Reuters said the airport authorities had advised passengers to contact their respective airlines before travelling to the airport and to check the latest status of their flights.
